description: In May 2002 Israel froze all processing of family unification applications with Palestinian spouses from the occupied territory. In August 2003 the moratorium was enshrined in law as a temporary order, on security grounds.
energy_note: A temporary order, twenty-three years old.

description: Israelis who marry foreigners who are not residents of the occupied territory may apply as before and the spouse can obtain status. The bar applies only to the one population.
energy_note: Marry anyone in the world. Except from there.

aspect: The outcomes for those inside the process
description: Between January 2000 and July 2013, 43% of family unification applications were rejected - 20% on security grounds, 13% for lack of proof of centre of life. Of 12,284 applications, 5,629 were approved and 4,249 rejected.
energy_note: Four in ten marriages, refused by a ministry.

aspect: Those who got through live on annual permits
description: The few who entered the process after the 2002 freeze live on temporary stay permits only - no stability, no social security rights, no health rights, and annual security vetting.
energy_note: Married, resident, and re-vetted every year.

description: Israel completely banned family unification with individuals from Gaza in 2008. For those couples there is no process to be refused by.

She has a blue Jerusalem ID, he has a green West Bank one. They married in 2009. He has never been permitted to live in the flat. He comes when a permit allows, which is not most weeks, and their daughter has worked out that asking when he is coming makes her mother go quiet.

Of 12,284 family unification applications between January 2000 and July 2013, 5,629 were approved and 4,249 rejected - a 43% rejection rate, 20% on security grounds and 13% for lack of proof of centre of life. Israel banned unification with individuals from Gaza outright in 2008.
energy_note: Four thousand two hundred and forty-nine marriages, refused.
